design.summary: Screens 12-24 of the iOS handoff are done, in the approved "Verdict first" direction. Cherry-picked the rescued WIP commit from origin/ios-parity-design-partial rather than restarting: its two .dc.html frames were already complete and are kept. Screens 12-18 (iPad regular width, 1194x834 at 390pt-scale) cover the 200pt sidebar with the fleet-switcher popover, Status 40/60, Log with the last-30 readings beside the steppers, Scans as the three-way review layout with the ◎ spotlight, Documents with a drag-from-Files drop target, History with the entry beside its scan, and Squawks with in-app resolve plus "which entry cleared it". Screens 19-24 cover Ask (regular pane + compact), the field editor (read chip, raw transcription beneath, 0.1 steppers), item editor and AD compliance, equipment install/remove and the meter-replacement prompt, document upload / attach picker / squawk resolve, and the conflict screen. New this session: docs/design/screens-12-24-ipad-and-editors.md — one spec in the handoff README's voice with purpose, pt-valued layout, copy, SF Symbol mapping and "what this fixes" per screen, and the light palette as a token table using tokens.ts names, framed as the answer t

requests.request: Add the light set to apps/mobile/src/tokens.ts under the SAME names, values from the token table in docs/design/screens-12-24-ipad-and-editors.md § "The light appearance": bg #F4F5F7 · surface #FFFFFF · surfaceRaised #ECEEF2 · hairline #D8DDE4 · ink #151A21 · dim #4A5462 · faint #666F7C · accent #1C6FD2 · accentLight #4A8FE3 · onAccent #FFFFFF · warning #9A6400 · danger #C4392C · success #177F55. Tints at the same alphas: accent #1C6FD21A / border #1C6FD24D, warning #9A64001A / #9A64004D, danger #C4392C1A / #C4392C4D, success #177F551A / #177F553D. useTheme() follows prefers-color-scheme. No size, radius, weight or gradient-direction change. The only non-token value that flips is the scrim over scan and PDF imagery: rgba(0,0,0,.42) dark → rgba(21,26,33,.28) light. Do not lighten `faint` back toward #77808E — it measures 3.7:1 on the light bg.

Sidebar 200pt fixed, surface, 1pt hairline right border, padding 18/12/16; nav rows 44pt, radius 11, 19pt icon + 11pt gap + 14.5/500 label; selected row surfaceRaised with accent label at 600. Order Status · Log · Records · Squawks, then an 8pt gap and Ask. A destination with attention shows a count (Space Grotesk 12/700, warning, or danger if anything there is grounding) that REPLACES the shortcut hint on that row; the shortcut still works. Account pinned to the bottom (margin-top:auto), 52pt, 30pt avatar, with a sync line that never says "queue": "Synced 4 min ago" / "Syncing…" / "Waiting for a connection". Full values in spec §12.

The fleet switcher is a popover anchored UNDER the tail, 300pt wide, surface, radius 16, 8pt padding, shadow 0 18 48 rgba(0,0,0,.45) — using screen 2's picker row idiom exactly (tail Space Grotesk 15/700, type 12 dim, status pill trailing, 52pt rows), a hairline, then "See the whole fleet" at 44pt in accent. Not a sheet.

TwoPane ratios from the frames: Status 40/60, Log 40/60, Documents 40/60, History 40/60, Squawks 40/60. Scans is the exception — spec §15 draws a 40% page rail plus a right pane itself split 55/45 into scan and entries. Two panes cannot express that; it needs a nested TwoPane or a third arrangement. Your call which, but the composition is load-bearing (it is the review layout the iPad exists for).
Shortcuts drawn in the frames and shown beside the sidebar rows: ⌘1–4 tabs, ⌘K Ask, ⌘N new squawk, ⌘←/⌘→ page, ⌘↩ confirm. Register through useShortcuts(map).

Field editor (spec §20): the read chip says "Uncertain read" (pill.due) or "Read clearly" (pill.ok) — never a percentage, never the word "confidence". The raw transcription sits DIRECTLY beneath the chip in a dashed-hairline block on bg, 14pt italic dim, with the doubt stated in words (e.g. '"3102.8" — the last digit could be a 3'). Meter fields are 46pt steppers stepping 0.1 with press-and-hold acceleration; text fields are 46pt inputs at 16pt. One primary ("Looks right" / "Save") plus ghosts "Blank it" and "Show on scan ◎". At regular width the crop step is dropped and the spotlight on the live scan STAYS LIT while the editor is open.

Scans review layout (spec §15): the ◎ spotlight is a 2pt accent rectangle over the read region with box-shadow 0 0 0 4px tint.accent, 0 0 24px tint.accentBorder. Field cells are 44pt, 2-column; an uncertain field carries tint.warning and its border; the field whose spotlight is lit gets an accent border and its locate button turns accent on tint.accent. Copy: "Check 1 field" not "1 low-confidence field"; "Re-read page" not "re-extract"; "Missed an entry?" not "add manual entry".

Meter-replacement prompt (spec §22a): a 290pt centred alert, fires on BLUR of the meter field, not per keystroke. Title "Lower than the last reading — was the tach replaced?", a delta line (2417.3 → 0.0) in Space Grotesk 20/700, then the plain explanation of what saying yes does. "Yes — new meter from today" is the primary; "I mistyped it" is the ghost and the common answer — it returns focus to the field with the text selected. Foot: "You can undo a meter swap from the reading list."

AD compliance sheet (spec §21a): the title is the AD's SUBJECT ("Seat rail wear") with the number as a 10pt tag beneath (AD 2011-10-09) — never a bare AD or FAR number as the title. Four 44pt state chips: Complied · Open · Doesn't apply · Superseded. Item editor (§21) shows the computed next-due BEFORE saving: "Next due works out to 3 Apr 2027. Change the interval and it moves."

Conflict screen (spec §24): a full screen at compact width, NOT a sheet — a sheet invites a swipe-away and this is a decision. Identical fields are shown unhighlighted so the two columns line up; only differing fields get tint.warning + border. "Decide later" is always present. Copy: "Yours"/"Theirs", never "local"/"remote"; "Changed in two places", never "merge conflict". At regular width it is a 560pt centred card over the dimmed tab, with column headers reading "· on this iPad".

Ask (spec §19): every answer ends in source chips naming the entry and page ("14 Mar 2026 · Airframe p.16"); the monthly allowance line sits on the composer where the cost is incurred ("Needs a connection · 14 of 50 questions left this month"), not in a profile. Never "AI", "model" or "tokens". Document upload (§23): the attach picker's primary NAMES the entry ("Attach to 14 Mar 2026") so the tap is unambiguous, with "No entry — keep it loose" as a ghost above it. Documents (§16): the drop target is a 2pt dashed accent border at −4pt inset over tint.accent; releasing opens the add sheet with the file already chosen.

The three design files are committed at docs/design/ in this repo but were NOT pushed to the Claude Design project — DesignSync returns "needs design-system authorization (/design-login)" for every method, which a subagent cannot run. After /design-login the push is: finalize_plan with projectId e6a4308f-b39c-4a63-a85f-9e650c333d0c, localDir = docs/design, writes = the three paths under design_handoff_ios_redesign/, deletes = [], then write_files with localPath for each. The files need no edits first.

blockers: DesignSync is unauthorized in this session — get_project and list_files both return "DesignSync needs design-system authorization. Run /design-login to authorize it with your claude.ai account", and a subagent cannot run /design-login. So the finalize_plan → write_files push to project e6a4308f-b39c-4a63-a85f-9e650c333d0c did not happen. All three files are committed to docs/design on ios-parity-design and are ready to push unchanged; the exact call sequence is in the PR body under Blocker.

The design-handoff README (design_handoff_ios_redesign/README.md) is only in the Claude Design project, so with DesignSync down I could not read it — the spec's voice is matched against docs/design/screen-11-scan-pages.md instead (same author, same direction), and the numbering of "open question #4" is taken from the stream brief rather than verified against the README. Worth a one-line check when someone next has DesignSync working: if #4 is not the light-appearance question, only the section heading needs renumbering.

CONTRACT §5 says the light set is owned by the platform stream and that streams "use token names only". I therefore specified the light values and did not edit apps/mobile/src/tokens.ts — the values are under "Requests for platform". If platform has already landed a light set with different values, mine should lose, except for `faint`: anything lighter than #666F7C drops 11.5pt metadata below 4.5:1 on the light bg.

Spec §15 (Scans, regular) needs a three-way split — a 40% page rail plus a right pane split 55/45 into scan and entries — which CONTRACT §5's TwoPane cannot express in one call. Flagged to the iPad shell as a nested TwoPane or a third arrangement. It is the one composition in the addendum that the shell's primitives do not already cover.
deviceChecklist: iPad, full screen, landscape and portrait: sidebar is 200pt in both, no tab bar anywhere.
iPad in Split View at ~507pt: falls back to the phone layout (breakpoint 700pt) — tab bar returns, no half-width two-pane.
Scans on iPad: page rail, scan and entries all on screen at once; tapping a field lights the ◎ spotlight over its region on the scan, and the spotlight STAYS LIT while the field editor is open.
Field editor: the raw transcription and the value are both readable at the default text size and at the largest Dynamic Type step; the editable field is ≥16px; − and + are ≥44pt.
Meter-replacement prompt: type a tach below the last reading and leave the field — the prompt appears exactly once (on blur, not per keystroke). "I mistyped it" returns focus with the text selected.

Conflict screen: force one by editing the same entry on the web while the phone is offline, then reconnect. Only the differing fields are highlighted; "Decide later" leaves it unresolved and it comes back.

Light appearance OUTDOORS in daylight: flip the system to light and read the 11.5pt metadata lines (faint) on Status and on a Log reading row. That is the value the #666F7C tuning was for — if it is unreadable in sun the palette is wrong, not the screen.
Colour-blind check: with the system's Colour Filters on, every status still reads — the words GROUNDED / DUE SOON / AIRWORTHY are present everywhere colour carries meaning.
Documents drag-and-drop: drag a PDF from Files onto the vault pane — the dashed drop target appears, and releasing opens the add sheet with the file already chosen.
Magic Keyboard: ⌘1–4 switch tabs, ⌘K opens Ask, ⌘N a new squawk, ⌘←/⌘→ page through scans, ⌘↩ confirms.
Squawk resolve on device: resolve one with a linked entry, then confirm the resolved row reads "Cleared <date> · <entry>" and that reopening it from the resolved list works.
Ask offline: open the pane with no connection and an existing thread — spec §19 leaves this state undrawn (see open question 3); whatever the build does, check it does not look broken.

status-ui.summary: Cherry-picked the rescued WIP commit, corrected three defects in it, and finished airworthiness management on the phone. AllItems (status-screen.tsx) is now a self-contained segmented Inspections · Directives · Equipment component that takes an aircraft, loads its own rows and needs no onBack, so the iPad shell can drop it straight into the Status right pane; "Mark done" renders in place rather than through a callback, so the pane needs no navigation of its own. Inspections get an ItemEditor sheet (mx.upsert/mx.delete), Mark done on every item, and mx.seedStandard for an aircraft tracking nothing. Directives list ad_compliance judged by the same @/lib/compliance the web uses, with a compliance sheet (ad.upsert/ad.delete/ad.track) and AD text from ad_reference when present, degrading to an online-only "read on the web" link with no new route. Equipment lists components with install/remove/reinstall/delete sheets linked to an entry and a proposals list with confirm/dismiss; both ad_reference and equipment_proposal degrade to empty until 0058. MeterResetPrompt plus a pure, tested detectBackwardsReading is delivered ready to wire. The two AI scans are online-only Bearer posts to the ex

requests.request: Wire MeterResetPrompt into record-screen.tsx where a reading is saved. Before enqueuing reading.create: const { meters } = await computeAirworthiness(aircraft.id); const cur = meter === 'hobbs' ? meters.hobbs : meter === 'airframe' ? meters.airframe : meters.tach; const hit = cur.estimated ? null : detectBackwardsReading([{ date: cur.asOf, value: cur[meter] }], value); if (hit) { setAskReset({ meter, prior: hit.prior, next: value }); return; } — compare against the CURRENT value, not raw hours_reading, because it already folds in log-entry readings and any earlier meter_reset; never prompt on an estimated value (bridged from the other meter, it cannot tell a swap from the ratio being off). Render <MeterResetPrompt aircraft meter={askReset.meter} prior={askReset.prior} next={askReset.next} date={date} onDecided={async (choice) => { setAskReset(null); if (choice !== 'cancel') await saveReading(); }} />. The reading must save AFTER the decision either way (the reset row has to exist first or the countdowns re-anchor a frame late); 'cancel' saves nothing. Full snippet in the PR body.

1) Replace the StatusAllItemsSlot placeholder body with `import { AllItems } from './status-screen'` and `return <AllItems aircraft={p.aircraft} onQueued={p.onQueued} />`, passing onQueued={h.onQueued} at the call site. 2) Pass onQueued to Status in both widths: <Status aircraft={aircraft} onComplete={…} onQueued={writeFinished} /> (compact) and onQueued={h.onQueued} (regular primary). Both are optional — without them AllItems falls back to its own drainActions() step, which works but does not pull, so nothing breaks if this lands late. 3) RecentReadingsSlot is labelled 'status-ui' in the shell but is not in this stream's brief and has not been built — it is unclaimed.

Two entry links the phone sends that the trust boundary silently discards, though both columns exist. In pickAdFields (compliance.ts) add to AdComplianceFields and to the returned object: reference_entry_id: typeof src.reference_entry_id === 'string' && src.reference_entry_id ? src.reference_entry_id : null. In pickComponentFields (equipment.ts) add the same shape for install_entry_id (markRemoved already accepts entryId for the removal side). Until these land the optimistic patch shows the link and the next pull takes it away. The sheets already send the right key names.

blockers: Contract §3 says ad.track takes `{id, reference, ...}` and the note 'the column is `reference`, not `ref`' is correct — the rescued WIP had `ref` and it is fixed. No contract change needed, but the WIP proves the trap is easy to fall into.

Schema mismatch, reported per the rules rather than fixed in someone else's file: ad_compliance.reference_entry_id and component.install_entry_id both exist, and both sheets offer 'the logbook entry that records this', but writes-c2's pickAdFields and pickComponentFields drop them at the trust boundary. Sent as a Request for writes C2. Until it lands the optimistic patch shows the link and the next pull removes it — cosmetic, not data loss.

Scans (mx.scan / equipment.scan) write server-side, and the phone's pull is owned by App.tsx's sync(); AllItems cannot trigger one without duplicating sync logic. The copy therefore says the results appear after the next sync rather than pretending they are already on the device. If the shell exposes a sync callback later, one line in runScanFor picks it up.

AllItems' fallback onQueued drains the action queue but does not pull, so a write made from the iPad pane before the shell request lands syncs up but does not refresh down until the next manual sync. Harmless; resolved by the iPad-shell request.

Branched off origin/ios-parity, which does not yet contain core-sync/writes-c1..c3/ipad-shell. Everything here was built against those branches' real interfaces (read via git show) but compiles against the stubs; MutationType is still `string` in the stub, so the union narrowing was verified by reading lib/sync/mutations.ts on core-sync rather than by the compiler. The proposals.${verb} template literal that would have broken under the real union is already fixed.
deviceChecklist: iPhone: Status → the bottom card ('Clear for now' / 'Everything tracked') → All items. Three segments; every row and the segment control comfortably tappable; nothing zooms when a field takes focus.

iPhone: Inspections → VOR check → Mark done, with place, bearing error, signature and logbook. The counter must reset immediately (before any sync), and after a sync THE WEB MUST SHOW A NEW LOG ENTRY carrying the place, the bearing error and the signature — 91.171(d), not just a moved date. This is the regression that matters most.
iPhone: airplane mode → mark an oil change done → kill the app → reopen → go back online. Exactly ONE entry and one counter reset (the mutation id doubles as the entry id).

iPhone: Inspections → + Add an inspection: months only, hours only, both, and neither. Each refusal must read like a sentence. Save one, reopen, edit the interval, delete it — each change shows on the row before the sync.
iPhone: an aircraft with no items → 'Set up the standard inspections' → annual, transponder, pitot-static and ELT appear after the sync.

iPhone: Directives → track '2023-04-08' → appears immediately as Open. Reopen, record compliance with date, hours, method and a linked entry. Sync, then confirm the web's compliance page shows the same record.

iPhone: Directives offline → 'Read the full directive on the web ›' is replaced by 'Reading the full text needs a connection'. An AD whose ad_reference is on the device still shows its title and abstract offline.

iPhone: Equipment → record an installation → mark it removed on a date with a linked entry → confirm on the web that a directive tied to that equipment flipped to 'does not apply' with the date and reason. Then 'Reinstalled'.

iPhone: meter-replacement round trip (needs the review-ui wiring): on Log enter a tach below the last reading → 'Lower than the last reading (4158.0)'. Choose 'Meter replaced' → sync → every hours countdown on Status still reads the same as before the swap. Repeat choosing 'It's right as typed' → the reading saves and no meter_reset row appears.
iPhone: both scan buttons offline → 'Reading your logs needs a connection', disabled. Online → a summary line, then the new rows after a sync.
iPhone: a view-only aircraft → no '+ Add', no 'Mark done', no scan buttons; opening a sheet says why it can't be saved.
iPad landscape: Status shows the verdict left and All items right with no back chevron. Tap Mark done in the right pane — it replaces the pane, not the whole screen, and returns to the list.
iPad half-split (compact): the same screen pushes, with the chevron back.
iPad: rotate with a sheet open — it stays open and stays reachable.
testsAdded: apps/web/test/mobile-status-logic.test.ts — 21 cases over status-logic.ts (apps/mobile has no runner)
detectBackwardsReading: flags a drop with the value it fell below; picks the latest reading BY DATE not last-in-array; null on empty/absent/NaN; a 0.1 drop still asks

review-ui.summary:
Cherry-picked the rescued WIP from origin/ios-parity-review-ui-partial (it compiled and its 14 tests passed as-is), audited it against the real schema and the finished writes-c1/c2/core-sync branches, fixed three real defects, and finished the two pieces it was missing.

Delivered: ReviewPane (entries on a page as cards, per-field "Check this" chip below the 0.75 threshold, ◎ per located field), SpotlightRing (ring + dim overlay drawn over PageViewer's image, positioned in percentages so it holds at any width/zoom), EntriesDrawer (compact — swipes up over the page viewer), PageReview (self-loading wrapper, the piece the iPad shell places beside PageViewer), and the EntryEditor sheet (native date picker, the shared Stepper extracted out of record-screen.tsx, page.ocr_text collapsed under the text fields, every editable control >=16px). Pages gains a "Needs a look · N" filter using @/lib/pageStatus (imported, not copied) plus "Confirm N clean" matching the server's isEntryClean. The Log tab gains "Recent readings" — last 30, tap to correct, swipe left to delete. Cmd-left/Cmd-right registered inside PageViewer (CONTRACT §11, the page index is its state) and Cmd-Return in ReviewPane. p

requests.request: Pass onQueued={writeFinished} to <PageViewer> and <Pages> in App.tsx. Both props are optional; without them a review write sits in the queue until the next scheduled sync instead of draining immediately.

Regular width: compose the review beside the scan. PageViewer already accepts review="external" (default "drawer" = today's phone behaviour), spot?: FieldBox|null and onPage?: (page: Page) => void. Hold the spotlight in the shell: const [spot, setSpot] = useState<{box: FieldBox|null; key: string|null}>({box:null,key:null}); const [shown, setShown] = useState<Page>(sub.pages[sub.index]); then <TwoPane ratio="55/45" primary={<PageViewer … review="external" spot={spot.box} onPage={(p) => { setShown(p); setSpot({box:null,key:null}); }} onQueued={writeFinished} />} secondary={<PageReview page={shown} onLocate={(box,key) => setSpot({box,key})} activeKey={spot.key} onQueued={writeFinished} />} />. PageReview and the Locate type are exported from ./review-pane.

After integration, replace the local useChords stand-in in review-pane.tsx with your useShortcuts from ./layout at its two call sites (ReviewPane and PageViewer), then delete useChords. The maps are already ShortcutMap-shaped. shortcuts.ts is vendored here verbatim from your branch (identical blob, merges to one file); useChords deliberately stays off your handler stack so nothing double-fires before the swap.

Optional, non-blocking: a seq-preserving patchRow(table, id, patch) on db.ts. review-local.ts writes optimistic patches through applyChanges (INSERT OR REPLACE), which resets the row's seq to 0 until the next pull rewrites it. Only getRows' ORDER BY seq notices and every review screen sorts its own rows, so nothing is broken today.

blockers: layout.tsx (iPad shell) is not on this branch, so useShortcuts could not be imported. shortcuts.ts is vendored verbatim from origin/ios-parity-ipad-shell (identical blob — the add/add merges to one file) and a five-line useChords in review-pane.tsx stands in. It reads chords through the shell's own chordOf, so the "⌘←/⌘→ keep their text meaning inside an input" rule is honoured, and it deliberately stays OFF the shell's handler stack so nothing fires twice after integration. Swap it out per request 3.
The iPad shell has not yet wired PageReview as the Pages secondary pane, nor passed onQueued to PageViewer/Pages. Both props are optional so nothing breaks before that lands — see requests 1 and 2.

base only works for reading.update / reading.delete once migration 0058 (core sync) is applied: hours_reading has no BEFORE UPDATE updated_at trigger before it. No new migration needed from this stream.

No agent can run this on a device. Everything gestural (drawer swipe, swipe-to-delete, spotlight accuracy on a real scan, the 16px keyboard-zoom trap) is covered by the device checklist rather than a test.

Scratchpad collision, resolved: the parallel status-ui agent overwrote the shared scratchpad file between my write and gh reading it, so PR #194 was created with #195's body. Corrected with gh pr edit; both PRs verified to carry their own body now. Worth giving parallel streams distinct scratchpad filenames next run.
deviceChecklist: iPhone — the three-page annual: Pages → "Needs a look" → open the page-15 scan, swipe the drawer up. Turn to page 16; its first entry must read "Continues from the previous page" and offer "Merge into the entry on the previous page". Merge 16→15 and 17→16. Expect one annual entry on page 15, nothing orphaned, and its equipment and AD links still attached (#188).

iPhone — confirm all clean: Pages → "Needs a look" → "Confirm N clean". Expect N to drop to just the entries the model was unsure about, the header count to match, and the web reviewer to agree after a sync.

iPhone — spotlight on a rotated page: open a page with sideways writing. Expect the warning line above the entries. Tap ◎ on a date and on a signature — the ring lands on the right ink, not the corner. Pinch-zoom: the ring stays on the value. A field the model couldn't place has no ◎ at all.

iPhone — editing offline: airplane mode, then edit an entry's tach, add a missed entry, confirm two entries, correct a reading in the Log tab, delete another. Each shows immediately and the note says "saved on this phone, uploads when connected". Reconnect and sync: everything lands, nothing duplicates, no edit is lost.

iPhone — conflict: edit an entry's description on the web while the phone holds an offline edit of the same entry, then reconnect. Expect the yours/theirs screen, not a silent overwrite in either direction.

iPhone — viewer access: sign in with view-only access to a shared aircraft. Expect no Confirm, no Delete, no editor sheet, no ◎-triggered writes, and the line "View-only access — nothing here can be changed."

iPhone — meters that aren't yours: Log tab → Recent readings. A MyFlightBook or ADS-B row must not open the editor and must not reveal Delete on a swipe; it reads "from MyFlightBook" / "from an ADS-B estimate".
iPhone — swipe then tap: swipe a manual reading left to reveal Delete. The same gesture must NOT also open the correction sheet. Tap the revealed row once to close it, tap again to edit.
iPhone — keyboard zoom trap: tap into the description field in the entry editor. Expect no zoom and no leftover pan after the keyboard closes.

iPhone — read this page: an unextracted page shows "Read this page · N of M left today". Tap offline → "Needs a connection — will read the page when you're back online". Online → entries arrive on the next sync. At the cap the button is disabled and reads "Daily limit reached (M pages)".
iPad — full screen with a page open: the review sits beside the scan, not in a drawer. Tap ◎ in the right pane → the ring appears in the left pane on the same page.

iPad — Magic Keyboard: ⌘→ / ⌘← turn the page and clear the spotlight; ⌘↩ confirms the next entry, and once none remain marks the page reviewed. Inside a text field ⌘← must still move the caret and NOT turn the page.
iPad — Split View at half width (under 700pt): the phone drawer comes back and nothing overlaps the bottom safe area.
testsAdded: apps/web/test/mobile-review-rules.test.ts — 15 node:test cases against the dependency-free apps/mobile/src/review-rules.ts
a page needs a look only when extracted AND holding an unconfirmed entry (reuses @/lib/pageStatus)
confirm-clean picks exactly what the server's confirmClean would (reuses isEntryClean)
field chips: only a doubtful field gets one, and it is a word not a percentage
entry badge reads in the owner's words
entriesOn keeps the order the entries appear on the page
validateEntry: a good form becomes the typed payload
validateEntry: the one thing to fix, in plain words (bad date, 2026-02-31 rollover, negative hours, empty description)
toForm round-trips nulls to empty strings
validateReading needs a real date and at least one meter
recent readings: newest first, capped at 30, same-day tie broken by created_at
allowance: read from the access response, degrade to the plain label
spotlight: percentages of the image, padded, clamped, and nothing for an unlocated field
drawer snaps only past the threshold; a wobble stays put
swipe-to-delete needs a clear leftward drag
only a hand-entered reading can be corrected on the phone (readingEditable / readingProvenance)

records-ui.summary: Shipped the records half of iOS parity in 5 commits on ios-parity-records-ui (PR #196 against ios-parity). Document upload: a filesystem-backed offline queue (blob-upload.ts — base64 bytes and metadata in separate files so listing what's waiting never reads a megabyte) draining JSON+base64 to the documents route writes-c3 made Bearer-capable, fed by a Files/iCloud/Photos picker, the existing VisionKit scanPages, and a drop target; photos downscaled, 25 MB cap enforced on-device. PageManager: sort by filed order/date/tach/AFTT through @/lib/pageSort (never a second copy of the ordering rules), up/down reorder everywhere plus HTML5 drag at regular width, multi-select bulk delete that names how many log entries go with the scans (#185's silent bulk delete), retake via the capture queue, and "keep this as the filed order" gated on displayedOrder so a page with no date can't silently renumber fifty others. Squawks gained a detail surface (sheet compact, right pane regular) with resolve + "which entry cleared it", reopen, edit and delete, swipe-to-resolve, and an openable Resolved list — all through enqueue() with the row's updated_at as base. Read-only W&B (with staleWBChanges as a reco

Creates device_token(token pk, user_id, platform, created_at) with owner-scoped select/delete RLS, plus register_device_token(p_token, p_platform) SECURITY DEFINER because registration cannot be an insert policy: when a phone already holding a row is signed into a second account, RLS hides the old row from the new owner, so neither an insert (PK collision) nor an upsert (its using clause matches nothing) can move it, and the previous owner would keep getting that phone's notifications. Migration 0058 updated_at audit: `squawk` has updated_at but NO set_updated_at trigger (0043) — add it, or the conflict check compares against the insert timestamp forever. `oil_addition` has no updated_at column at all (0042).

CONTRACT §3 marks `oil.delete (base)` but oil_addition has no updated_at and no update path; oil.deleteTopOff accepts `base` and ignores it. Drop '(base)' from that row or have 0058 add the column+trigger.

CONTRACT §3 says `aircraft.enroll` 'route made Bearer' but no enroll route existed (server action only). Created POST /api/aircraft/enroll — confirm writes-C3 ownership or reassign. Also add lib/writes/aircraft.ts to the §8 ownership table.

POST /api/aircraft/[id]/backup/run semantics are 'runs with tonight's sweep' (pulls next_run_at forward; the archive only builds under the cron's service credentials), not 'runs now'; once per day per destination. Reflect in the plan/help copy.

Document upload: POST /api/aircraft/[id]/documents with Content-Type application/json, body {file:<base64>, fileName, mimeType, type?, title?, reference?, document_date?, notes?, log_entry_id?}; max 25 MB decoded; PDF/JPEG/PNG/WebP; response {ok, document}. Back up now: POST /api/aircraft/[id]/backup/run → 400 'Set up a cloud backup in your profile first.', 429 'A backup already ran in the last day.', ok → show `message`.

blockers: Contract/schema mismatch: §3 `oil.delete (base)` — oil_addition has no updated_at column (0042); base is accepted but cannot be compared. Needs a contract edit or 0058 to add the column.
squawk has updated_at but no set_updated_at BEFORE UPDATE trigger (0043) — squawk conflict detection is ineffective until 0058 (core sync) adds it.
Contract §3 references an 'aircraft.enroll route' that did not exist; created POST /api/aircraft/enroll outside the §8 ownership list — needs lead confirmation.

No safe inline backup trigger exists (the runner is the cron sweep under service credentials in api/cron/backup, not lib/backup); backup/run schedules the next sweep instead of building the archive on request.
Branch is stacked on #189 (origin/ios-parity-writes-c1 merged in) because the shared WriteResult/WriteCtx helpers live in lib/writes/entries.ts; merge #189 first.

POST /api/sync/push dispatch table rows for the 18 C2 types (reading.create/update/delete, meterReset.create/delete, mx.upsert/delete/complete/seedStandard, ad.upsert/delete/track, component.upsert/delete/remove/reinstall, proposals.confirm/dismiss) — the exact payload→function mapping is in the PR body; inserts get the mutation id spread in as `id`, mx.complete gets it as `entryId`.
CONTRACT §3: ad.track payload `{id, ref, ...}` → `{id, reference, kind?, title?, applicability?, recurring?, intervalHours?, intervalMonths?, nextDueDate?, nextDueHours?}` (column is `reference`).

CONTRACT §3: mx.complete payload `{itemId, date, hours?, notes?, signature?, logbookId?}` → `{itemId, date?, hours?, logbookId?, description?, workPerformed?, signature?, tach?, hobbs?}` — `notes` is not a log_entry column; the 91.171(d) record needs description + workPerformed (+ meters), which the phone already builds.
CONTRACT §3: component.remove payload `date` is optional in the implementation (absent ⇒ today, matching the web).

CONTRACT §3: mx.upsert / ad.upsert / component.upsert inserts carry no id ("base when id present" ⇒ id means update), so a phone retry after a lost response can double-insert. Decide whether to change to "id always present; base present ⇒ update".

blockers: Contract/schema mismatch: §3 ad.track names the field `ref`; the real column and existing actions use `reference` — implemented as `reference`.

Contract/schema mismatch: §3 mx.complete carries `notes`, which is not a log_entry column; the 91.171(d) record needs `description` + `workPerformed` (+ `tach`/`hobbs`) — implemented with those names (MarkDoneInput).
